prompt:

Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. Her element — ytterbium: a soft, ductile, bright silvery metal named for the Swedish village of Ytterby, separated in 1878 in Geneva from erbia, with its younger sister lutetium still hidden inside it until 1907; held one by one in an egg-crate lattice of light, its atoms tick to a steady yellow laser more than five hundred trillion times a second in optical clocks so exact they would not lose a second over the age of the universe and can feel time run faster when lifted a few centimetres, the likely successor to the caesium second; squeezed hard, its electrical resistance rises, so it gauges the pressure of earthquakes and blasts; inside glass fibre it powers the invisible infrared lasers that cut steel — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
